company_guide.title: Company Guide
company_guide.subtitle: How to structure your business — whether it's one location or several, run entirely by you, or shared with family, partners, or franchisees.

single_business.title: Every business stands on its own
single_business.body: A business in FlairSync is one physical location — its own menu, its own floor plan, its own staff, its own settings. Whoever creates it owns it, with full control over everything inside.

multi_business.title: Running more than one location yourself
multi_business.body: If you personally run more than one location, you don't need a second account — create every location under your own login, and use the business switcher in the sidebar to jump between them any time. Just make sure your subscription plan is sized for your total number of locations and combined staff count, not just one — limits are counted across every business you own, together.

staff_roles.title: Bringing on managers and staff
staff_roles.body: Every business has its own team, set up independently of any other location you own. Add a staff member, then build a Role for them — Manager, Head Chef, Waiter, whatever fits — and choose exactly what they can see and do: menu, orders, staff, reports, POS actions, and more. "Manager" isn't a special system concept; it's a Role you define yourself, and it only applies to that one business. Running several locations means setting this up separately for each one.

org_region.title: When locations belong to different owners
org_region.body: Sometimes a location isn't run by you personally — a family member, a business partner, or an independent franchisee owns and runs it under their own account. You can still see it alongside your own locations by creating an Organization or a Region and inviting that business to link in.
org_region.body_consent: Linking is always a two-way agreement — nobody can pull another business into their organization without that business's owner approving it, and it never hands over any control. An Organization or Region owner sees combined sales, order counts, low-stock alerts, and labor cost across every linked location — never anyone else's menu, staff, or settings. Either side can request to leave at any time.
org_region.example: A parent who built up three family restaurants, now each run day-to-day by a different adult child. Each child has their own account and owns their own location outright. The parent creates a Region, and each child links their business into it — the parent gets one combined view of how the family's restaurants are doing, without ever touching a sibling's day-to-day decisions.

items.then: Just create each one under your account — no Organization needed.

items.if: I'm hiring managers to run locations for me
items.then: Keep every location under your account, and give each manager a Role scoped to their site.

items.if: Someone else owns and runs a location, but I want visibility into it
items.then: Create an Organization or Region and send that business a link request.

items.if: I want combined reporting across locations owned by different people
items.then: Same as above — an Organization or Region, once every side approves.

explainer.title: What's an Organization?
explainer.description: The top of your multi-location structure. It can hold branches directly, or hold whole Regions — each grouping their own branches underneath. You own it, and every link works in either direction: invite a branch or region in, or approve one that asks to join. Nothing links without approval, and leaving works the same way in reverse.

regions_page.title: Regions

regions_page.empty_description: Managing a cluster of branches? Create a region to group them, whether or not they're part of a larger organization yet.

explainer.title: What's a Region?
explainer.description: A cluster of branches under one regional manager. A region stands fully on its own — it doesn't need an organization above it — but can link up to one later if you want it rolled into a bigger group. Linking and leaving both require the other side's approval, the same as everywhere else in this structure.
